chapter: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
title: Sawdust Trail, the Lone Star and Sunset crowd
summary: Musicians ate breakfast at Sawdust Trail; the Lone Star with Pete Johnson and Joe Turner was classier than the Sunset.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Uh, I think they both were three years older than me, not more than four years older, three years older than me, I think. But, you know, they noticed that I wasn't a heckler--Why you do it? How you do that? You know. I'd just stand there and listen to them, you know. And we'd go across, and there was a place where all the musicians would meet called Sawdust Trail. And we'd go across there sometime 9:00 o'clock in the morning.
Was that a bar?
No, that was a dining room.
Oh.
But they had sawdust on the floor.
(laughter)
And so all the musicians would meet there. And now, directly across from Sunset was the Lone Star, where Pete Johnson was playing, later joined by Joe Turner, you see.
Lone Star, that was what--a bar?
That was a nightclub, but that was more like--that's, oh, that was a place maybe--that was a place kinda like Jimmy Ryan's here in New York.
Oh, I see. Yeah.
Where there was seats and things like that, and what's-'er-name--
Well, who, what would the audience be there? Would that be mostly white, or--
Oh, you'd find whites all over. In the black neighborhood, they didn't object to 'em; they let 'em--you know, they'd mingle like that. No black was minglin' with a white woman, you know.
Well, what about the Sunset? Would that be a rule?

Yeah. But now Sunset was busy, like a bucket of blood. Not a bucket of blood--somewhere, it was crowded all the time, and you might see somebody fightin' in there, you had to break out of there (laugh).
Yeah. In other words, the Lone Star was a little better.
Yeah, it was class.
Than the Sunset?
Yeah. And so we would stop over there for breakfast, and they'd get us home, you know, back to college. And we'd go quite often.
Well, at this time, we're talking of what--'33?

Yeah, 'cause I went there in '32, so I'd say end of '33, 'cause I -- yeah, it was '33 'cause there was a movie--I remember one time I went over there and got there too early, so I went to the movie next door
And it had a movie, Fred McMurray and some kind of Pines.
Trail of the Lonesome Pines.
Yes.
Yeah, I remember seeing that.
Yeah. And we went.
It was supposed to be quite good.
Yeah, I liked it, you know.
Yeah.
I went back to see it again.
Well, anyway, it was in the lumber country, as I remember or something like that.
